title: Setting out: пойти, поехать — and сходить, съездить

blocks.text: The perfective aspect of "Going Verbs" is formed by adding the prefix "**по**" to the actual function verbs ("**идти**", "**ехать**", etc.). The perfective verbs **пойти** and **поехать** denote a single action with emphasis on the completed start. (Similar to the English concept of "to leave for"; "to set out").

items: Где старшина?
Where is the M/Sgt?
Он пошёл в штаб.
He went to (left for) HQ.

blocks.text: Note. — that the vowel **-ё-** in the verb "**пойти**" occurs in the masculine form only: **пошёл**, **пошла**, **пошло**, **пошли**. The future perfective (**пойду**, **пойдёшь**) belongs to the 1st **-ё-** type of conjugation. The future perfective (**поеду**, **поедешь**) belongs to the 1st **-е-** type of conjugation.

The perfective verb **полететь** (like **пойти** and **поехать**) denotes single action with the emphasis on the completed start. The past perfective (**полетел**, **-ла**, **-ло**, **-ли**) is formed in a regular way.
The future perfective (**полечу**, **полетишь**) belongs to the 2nd (**-и-**) type of conjugation. The consonant "**т**" changes into "**ч**" in the first person singular only.

items: Полковник полетел в Вашингтон.
The Colonel flew to Washington. (single action; completed start)
Завтра я полечу на фронт.
Tomorrow I'll fly to the front. (single action)

blocks.text: The addition of the prefix **по-** to a unidirectional verb of motion makes the verb perfective, denoting the beginning of a movement, i.e. 'setting out'. These perfectives imply that the agent has not yet returned at the moment of speech, e.g.:

items: Он пошёл к другу.
He went to a friend's place (and has not returned; unidirectional perfective).
Он шёл к другу.
He was on his way to a friend's place (unidirectional imperfective).
Он ходил к другу.
He used to go to a friend's place (multidirectional).
Он сходил к другу.
He went to a friend's place (and has returned; see prefixed perfective forms of motion verbs below).

по- and с- with ходить, ездить, летать

Adding a prefix to the repeated function verbs: **ходить**, **ездить**/**езжать**/, **летать** usually does not form the perfective aspect but merely changes the meaning of the original verb: **ходить** — to go, **уходить** — to leave. However, prefixes "**по**-" and "**с**-" may form the perfective aspect with the "repeated function" verbs.

a) Prefix "**по**-" denoting a perfective action of limited duration (an action "for a while"). The prefix "**по**-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — **ходить**, **ездить**, **летать** — forms perfective verbs: **походить**, **поездить**, **полетать**.
These verbs denote a single completed action of limited duration, similar to the verb "**погулять**".

items: Он походил по комнате и сел за стол.
Мы поездили по городу и поехали домой.
Я хочу полетать на самолёте.

blocks.text: b) Prefix "**с**-" implying a single round trip. The prefix "**с**-" when added to the "repeated function" verbs — **ходить**, **ездить**, **летать** — forms perfective verbs: **сходить**, **съездить**, **слетать**.
These verbs denote a single trip (going to and coming from a place), especially when a quick return is implied.

items: Мне надо сходить на почту за письмами.
Я съезжу на вокзал и узнаю, когда отходит поезд.
Он сходил в библиотеку и взял книгу.

blocks.text: Note the preposition: after "going verbs" or the verb "to send" the preposition "**за**" + Instr. is used to indicate the idea of "going after" or "sending for" something or somebody: **Он пошёл за газетой**. — He went after the newspaper. **Пошлите за доктором**. — Send for the doctor.

exercises.why: **побежали** — past tense (plural) of побежать: the perfective of бежать, «set out».

exercises.q: Let's run to the bus stop.
exercises.why: **побежали** — past tense (plural) of побежать: the perfective of бежать, «set out».
**побежал** — past tense (masculine) of побежать: the perfective of бежать, «set out».

exercises.q: Tom ran to get a doctor.
exercises.why: **побежал** — past tense (masculine) of побежать: the perfective of бежать, «set out».
**полетел** — past tense (masculine) of полететь: the perfective of лететь, «set out».

exercises.q: They swam out to the island.
exercises.why: **поплыли** — past tense (plural) of поплыть: the perfective of плыть, «set out».

exercises.q: Хочу ___ (полететь — to fly off) на Марс.
exercises.why: **полететь** — infinitive, the perfective of лететь, «set out».
exercises.prompt: I want to go to Mars.

exercises.q: Я хочу ___ (полететь — to fly off) на Луну.
exercises.why: **полететь** — infinitive, the perfective of лететь, «set out».
exercises.prompt: I want to travel to the moon.

exercises.q: Ты ___ (поплавать — to swim for a while) с Томом?
exercises.why: **поплаваешь** — future tense (2nd person singular) of поплавать: the perfective of плавать meaning «for a while».

exercises.q: Ден и Линда ___ (полететь — to fly off) в Лондон.
exercises.why: **полетели** — past tense (plural) of полететь: the perfective of лететь, «set out».
exercises.prompt: Dan and Linda flew to London.

exercises.q: Собака ___ (побежать — to start running) за лисой.
exercises.why: **побежала** — past tense (feminine) of побежать: the perfective of бежать, «set out».
exercises.prompt: The dog ran after a fox.

exercises.q: Я собираюсь ___ (поплавать — to swim for a while).
exercises.why: **поплавать** — infinitive, the perfective of плавать meaning «for a while».

exercises.q: Пошли ___ (поплавать — to swim for a while) в реке.
exercises.why: **поплаваем** — future tense (1st person plural) of поплавать: the perfective of плавать meaning «for a while».
exercises.prompt: Let's go and swim in the river.

exercises.q: Не ___ (сбегать — to run there and back) с концерта!
exercises.why: **сбегайте** — imperative (вы, plural or polite) of сбегать: the perfective of the many-directions verb, meaning one trip there and back.
exercises.prompt: Don't sneak out of the concert!
